paper_metadata.title: Reliable HEC joints with distinctive high-entropy heterogeneous interfaces fabricated by employing a CCFN alloy

evidence.quote: The liquid CCFN did not undergo phase separation and was retained in the brazing seam, forming the HEC joint with a high-entropy interfacial structure.

evidence.section: 4. Conclusions
evidence.quote: Reliable HEC joints with distinctive high-entropy heterogeneous interfaces had been successfully fabricated by employing a CCFN alloy, and the evolution of the interfacial structure in response to brazing process parameters has been elucidated.

evidence.section: 3.3. Mechanical properties of HEC joints brazed with CCFN alloy
evidence.quote: The joint strength remained in the extent of 201 – 220 MPa when the bonding temperatures exceeded 1460 ◦C

evidence.section: 3.3. Mechanical properties of HEC joints brazed with CCFN alloy
evidence.quote: the failure location of the joint moved from the HEC substrate to the dissolution zone, where the dissolution, interfacial reaction, and atomic interdiffusion between the HEC and CCFN proceeded sufficiently over a longer time of 45 min.

evidence.section: 3.3. Mechanical properties of HEC joints brazed with CCFN alloy
evidence.quote: For the fracture behavior of the joints subjected to shear loading at RT, it was reasonable that the cracks occurred and propagated in the HEC since the brittleness of HEC is much higher than that of CCFN alloy.

samples.original_name: HEC/CCFN/HEC joint brazed at 1460 °C for 45 min

evidence.section: 3.3. Mechanical properties of HEC joints brazed with CCFN alloy
evidence.quote: With a prolonged bonding time of 60 min, the cracks in the HEC propagated through the narrower CCFN layer in the brazing seam, which was a consequence of the strength of the HEC joint being higher than that of the HEC substrate.

samples.original_name: HEC/CCFN/HEC joint brazed at 1440 °C for 15 min

evidence.section: 3.3. Mechanical properties of HEC joints brazed with CCFN alloy
evidence.quote: For a shorter bonding time of 15 min, the inferior strength of 140 MPa was probably ascribed to the presence of large residual stresses within the HEC near the brazing seam as a large amount of liquid CCFN remained in the joint.

evidence.section: 3.3. Mechanical properties of HEC joints brazed with CCFN alloy
evidence.quote: The highest strength of 266 MPa could be obtained for the joint brazed at 1460 ◦C for 45 min.

evidence.section: 3.3. Mechanical properties of HEC joints brazed with CCFN alloy
evidence.quote: A similar circumstance also appeared in the joints obtained at the lower temperature of 1440 ◦C.

evidence.section: 4. Conclusions
evidence.quote: The Zr atoms in the liquid CCFN served as active atoms and induced the formation of ZHEC phases dependent on the dissociated HEC grains, which was characterized by the increased Zr content to 21.44 at.% and the coherent orientation with the HEC.

evidence.section: 4. Conclusions
evidence.quote: Due to the low solid solubility of Hf and Zr atoms in liquid CCFN, a certain amount of twinned Laves phases were formed in the brazing seam, where the liquid CCFN did not occur phase separation after solidification, resulting in a high-entropy interfacial structure of HEC/CCFN/HEC.

evidence.section: 3.3. Mechanical properties of HEC joints brazed with CCFN alloy
evidence.quote: At 800 ◦C, the joint strength was 107 MPa, which was merely 40.2 % of the value tested at RT.

evidence.section: 3.3. Mechanical properties of HEC joints brazed with CCFN alloy
evidence.quote: The joint under 1000 ◦C still retained a shear resistance of 85 MPa, and the result confirmed a sound potential for high-temperature service.

evidence.section: 4. Conclusions
evidence.quote: When the joint was tested at 1000 ◦C, the strength value still retained 87 MPa, indicating a positive potential for high-temperature applications, where intergranular fracture of the CCFN caused the joint failure.

evidence.section: 4. Conclusions
